newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU proposes ban on S.African ostrich exports.
newsitem.headline: EU proposes ban on S.African ostrich exports.

text.p: The European Union's standing veterinary committee has proposed a ban on the export of ostrich meat and live ostriches from South Africa after an outbreak of Congo fever, South African health officials said on Thursday.

The Health Department in Pretoria said the ban had been proposed as a precautionary measure, "due to the uncertainty about the safty of ostrich meat for human consumption in the event of an outbreak of Congo fever".
Up to 17 people working at an ostrich abattoir are feared to have contracted the tick-borne fever. One of them has died.

Congo-Crimean haemorrhagic fever is an infectious disease that, like the more notorious viral disease Ebola, causes body organs to degenerate with massive internal and some external bleeding. About 30 percent of Congo fever cases are fatal.

South Africa has undertaken to conduct urgent research to clarify uncertainties over ostrich meat, with agreement that the EU shall review its call for a ban once scientific evidence confirms the disease cannot be spread through ostrich meat.

But the health department said South Africa would lodge an official objection with the EU requesting the reasons for extending the ban to the country's entire ostrich industry even though the outbreak was confined to one abattoir.
South Africa's first confirmed case of Congo fever was in 1981 in a boy bitten by a tick and since then there have been sporadic cases, mainly in rural areas.
